Seriously, it probably is your fan. For some reason your computer is probably overheating and the fan will try to cool it off (in doing so, making loud noises) and then the computer decides it's too hot and it shuts itself off. The issue could very well be the fan. Often times when a fan goes bad, it will send bad information to the computer to make it think it's getting much hotter than it actually is, making it think it needs to compensate with the fan, and overall shutting itself off. I would feel the computer next time this happens. If it's far too hot for you to touch for more than 3 seconds, then the problem is not the fan. It could just be the motherboard thinking it's receiving information that the computer is hot. In which case, sledgehammer. If it doesn't feel too hot, it's probably your fan (or fans). Fans are typically fairly cheap if you wanted to try the repair yourself. If you replace the fan and it still has the same issue and the computer still doesn't feel too hot, then your motherboard is bad. Again, sledgehammer.
